input.question: Why can't you parallel park going forward?
input.ground_truth: I think it's because front wheels turn but rear wheels don't. When you're parallel parking, you use your front wheels to point the back of your car at the curb, and your rear wheels end up parallel to it. If you're driving in forward, the rear of your car is still pointed to the street, and it takes a lot more maneuvering to turn them toward the curb. By comparison, if you're pulling up next to a curb with no cars around you, you turn your front wheels to the curb, then turn them parallel to the curb, and your rear wheels follow and align. But you don't have nearly enough space to do that when parallel parking.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why can't you parallel park going forward?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy car and you want to park it between two big blocks, but there isn’t much space.

If you try to drive the car straight (forward) into the space, the car will bump into the block in front of the spot. That’s not good!

But if you turn the wheels a little (called “steering”) and drive backwards a tiny bit while turning, the car can slide into the space between the blocks. That’s called “parallel parking.”

So, you can’t parallel park going forward because you need to move backwards a little to fit the car into the tight spot. It’s like backing into a parking spot between two big trucks!
